mainEntity.name: Does the editor check my XML?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. It uses the browser's own XML parser and shows the first well-formedness error with its line and column, plus undeclared namespace prefixes and ids that are used twice. It does not validate against a DTD or an XML Schema.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to open XML with a DTD or external entities?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The editor never loads a DTD, a schema or an external entity and never expands entities from a DTD, so XXE and entity expansion attacks do not work. References to such entities stay in the text as they are written.

Type an XPath 1.0 expression above the tree, for example //book[price > 30]/title. The matching nodes are marked in the tree; the arrows go from one to the next. Prefixes declared in the document work, and _: stands for the default namespace of the root element.

mainEntity.name: Can I convert XML to JSON or YAML?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Under Convert or Export, the document becomes JSON or YAML: attributes as @name, text as #text, repeated elements as lists.

Only in your browser. Click the folder button at the top left (My documents) to open, rename, duplicate, download or delete them. Clearing your browser's site data removes them, so download the ones you want to keep - or let the editor send them to your own server ("Save to server").

mainEntity.name: Can an AI write in the XML Editor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, any AI - ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot or the AI in your coding tool. Click "AI Assistant", then "Copy prompt", paste it into your AI and say what it should write. The AI answers with a link; click it and the document appears in your editor. "Undo" takes every change back.

mainEntity.name: Can I use the editor on my own website?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Embed it with an iframe and exchange documents with postMessage, or let it send every saved version to your server with a webhook. See Use the editor on your own website for examples.

mainEntity.name: Does the XML Editor cost anything?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The editor is free, without ads and without sign-up.

page_text:
Edit XML online, with a live tree

The XML Editor shows your code and its element tree side by side. Whatever you type appears in the tree right away - elements, attributes, text, comments, CDATA and namespaces - and a click on any node takes you to its place in the code. You can also edit names, values and text right in the tree, run XPath queries and convert the document to JSON or YAML.

Everything runs in your browser. Your documents are kept there, not on our server, and there is no sign-up and no advertising.

What the editor can do

Code with highlighting

Tags, attributes, values, entities, comments and CDATA in their own colors, line numbers, end tags that close by themselves and a clear list of problems with line and column.

The element tree

Fold and unfold elements, see attributes, text, comments, processing instructions and namespaces, and follow the path of the selected node.

Edit in the tree

Rename elements and attributes, change values and text, add, move and remove elements - written into the code as small edits, with special characters escaped.

XPath and search

An XPath 1.0 field marks the matching nodes; the search finds names, values and text. Namespace prefixes of the document work in XPath.

Safe with any file

No DTD, schema or external entity is ever loaded and no entity is expanded, so XXE and entity bombs do not work.

Format and convert

Indent or minify the document, or turn it into JSON or YAML: attributes as @name, text as #text, repeated elements as lists.

How it works

  1. Start - choose a template under "New", open an .xml file or paste XML code.
  2. Edit - type in the code or click values in the tree; the problems above the code tell you what is not well-formed.
  3. Export - save the XML, a minified copy, JSON, YAML or the plain text.

Use the editor on your own website

Put the editor into your own website with an iframe or in a window of its own. Your page hands it the document, gets every change and every save back, and can let an AI send its results to your server. No sign-up, no key.

embed.h1: Embed the XML Editor in your website
embed.intro: For developers: how to put the XML Editor into your own page - in an iframe, in a window of its own or as a read-only viewer - and how documents, saves and AI results travel between the editor and your server. You need no sign-up and no key from us.
embed.body:
Any https page (and localhost) can embed the editor with an <iframe> and ?embed=1 - no sign-up, no key. Embedded, the editor hides the page text and shows a Save button. There are four ways to get the document in and out.

1. Open a file from a link, save to your server

src= opens a file (your server must allow CORS), webhook= makes "Save" (Ctrl+S) send the document to that address. Add &auto to save after every change.

<iframe src="https://xml.giit.ch/?embed=1&src=https://your-site.com/data/catalog.xml&webhook=https://your-site.com/save.php"
        allow="clipboard-write" style="width:100%;height:800px;border:0"></iframe>

The webhook gets a POST with JSON { editor: "xml", event: "save", id, name, content, updated }. A link carries no token (it would end up in server logs and the browser history), so a webhook in the address suits a save address that needs none, for example on localhost or in your intranet. For a public server, hand the webhook over with a token in xmleditor:load (hook: { url, token }) and check it, as this small PHP script does:

<?php
header('Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://xml.giit.ch');
header('Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Authorization');
header('Access-Control-Allow-Methods: POST, OPTIONS');
if ($_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] === 'OPTIONS') exit;
if (($_SERVER['HTTP_AUTHORIZATION'] ?? '') !== 'Bearer SECRET') { http_response_code(403); exit; }
$d = json_decode(file_get_contents('php://input'), true);
$name = preg_replace('/[^\w\- ]/u', '_', $d['name']);
file_put_contents(__DIR__ . "/data/$name.xml", $d['content']);
echo '{"ok":true}';

2. Your page holds the document (postMessage)

The editor says xmleditor:ready, your page answers with xmleditor:load, the editor reports xmleditor:loaded, xmleditor:change on real edits and xmleditor:save when the user saves. Your page may send xmleditor:get (the current state) or xmleditor:save (press Save). Saving then goes through your own login and session.

<iframe id="ed" src="https://xml.giit.ch/?embed=1" allow="clipboard-write" style="width:100%;height:800px;border:0"></iframe>
<script>
const ed = document.getElementById('ed');
const ORIGIN = 'https://xml.giit.ch';

addEventListener('message', async e => {
  if (e.source !== ed.contentWindow || e.origin !== ORIGIN) return;
  const m = e.data;
  if (m.type === 'xmleditor:ready') {               // the editor is ready: hand it the document
    ed.contentWindow.postMessage({
      type: 'xmleditor:load',
      name: 'Catalog',
      content: await (await fetch('/data/catalog.xml')).text()
    }, ORIGIN);
  }
  if (m.type === 'xmleditor:change') document.title = '● not saved';     // a real edit
  if (m.type === 'xmleditor:save') {                // the user clicked "Save"
    await fetch('/api/save', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ name: m.name, content: m.content }) });
    document.title = 'Saved';
  }
});

// A save button on your own page: the answer comes as xmleditor:save
function saveNow() { ed.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'xmleditor:get' }, ORIGIN); }
</script>

AI Assistant inside your page: it works in the frame too. With allow="clipboard-write" on the iframe, "Copy prompt" uses the clipboard directly (otherwise the editor falls back to the old copy command, or shows the prompt to copy by hand). A link the AI sends cannot reach an editor inside another website, so the editor tells the AI and the user to paste the AI's whole answer into the editor instead - or open the editor in a window of its own.

3. In a window of its own

window.open("https://xml.giit.ch/?embed=window", "xmleditor-17") opens the full editor in its own window and speaks the same messages with window.opener. Links from an AI reach it there. xmleditor:load may also carry context: { host, title, rules } - the AI prompt then says where the document belongs and follows your rules - and hook: { url, token }, a webhook for this document only that is never stored. Closing the window with unsaved changes sends xmleditor:closing.

4. AI through your own server

Hand the editor your own prompt, an address on your site and a key for this editor session. The AI dialog then shows "Connected to" your site, what you tell the AI, and the choice change the current document or make a new one; Copy prompt puts it all together. The AI posts its result with the key to your server, and your page opens it in the editor - a new document opens separately and stays in the user's browser. One key per editor session: it stays valid while the editor is open, and only while it has none the editor asks for it with xmleditor:key-request. The editor never sends the key itself and never stores it; the address must be https on your own host or a subdomain of it.

const key = async () => (await fetch('/api/ai-key.php?doc=17')).json();   // one key per editor session
const k = await key();
ed.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'xmleditor:load', name: 'Catalog', content, ai: {
  label: 'My Site', prompt: 'Keep the sku attributes. Prices in CHF.',
  endpoint: 'https://your-site.com/api/ai-result.php', key: k.key } }, ORIGIN);
// remember the id from xmleditor:loaded and ignore change/save/closing with another id
// only while the editor has no key:
if (m.type === 'xmleditor:key-request') { const k = await key(); ed.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'xmleditor:ai', key: k.key }, ORIGIN); }
// while the editor is open, tell your server every minute; closing the editor or the page voids the key
setInterval(() => fetch('/api/ai-key.php?alive=' + k.key.slice(0, 8)), 60000);
// your server has a result (polling, SSE …): target is "current" or "new"
ed.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'xmleditor:load', name: 'Catalog', content: draft, from: 'ai', target }, ORIGIN);

Make keys with at least 128 random bits, store only their hash, bind each to the logged-in user, the document and this editor session, make one per session, keep it valid only while your page reports the session as open, and void it when the editor or the page closes.

The whole protocol is in llms.txt - give it to an AI and it builds the connection for your system. The other giit editors work the same way with their own prefix - editors.giit.ch.

Show a document read-only (viewer)

?viewer=1 shows only the finished document: no code, no tools, nothing can be changed, and nothing is stored in the browser. The document comes from a link (#b64=, ?src=), from your page with xmleditor:load, or by POST as a normal form to post.php: the field content as text or b64 as base64, optionally name, at most 20 MB of text.

<form method="post" action="https://xml.giit.ch/post.php?viewer=1" target="_blank">
  <input type="hidden" name="name" value="Report">
  <input type="hidden" name="b64" value="…">
  <button>Open</button>
</form>

Without viewer=1 the document opens in the normal editor. Either way it is kept in memory only: it is not stored on the server and does not join "My documents". Opened directly, the viewer says that the content comes from a third party.
